## Your environment
- You are at the root of an isolated git worktree of cfanalytics, detached at the head of the branch build/compat, which is master with waves 1 to 3 built. pleach runs you and checks your work with the gate named below.
- Leave your work uncommitted. Do not create branches, commit or push. Never touch Cloudflare: everything runs against `wrangler dev` on this machine.
- Delete with `trash`, never `rm`. A run may `rm` a temp folder that the same run created.
- If something stops you that you cannot fix inside your own files, write BLOCKED.md at the repository root: what is wrong, where, and what would fix it. Then stop.

## Read first
- CLAUDE.md, docs/engineering.md (above all "Real SDKs" and "A run leaves nothing behind"), docs/spec/posthog-protocol.md, and decisions D-13, D-15, D-19 and D-20 in docs/decisions.md.
- docs/reviews/2026-10-20-spike-s2.md: spike S2 ran these same SDKs against a spike Worker and lists what each needs (findings 1 to 7). Its code is on the branch spike/s2: read it with `git show spike/s2:spikes/s2/<path>`, for example `run.mjs`, `checks.mjs`, `clients/node.mjs`, `clients/browser.mjs`, `clients/macos.mjs`, `pages/*` and `macos/*`. Port what fits; do not copy its debug dump, since the real Worker has none.
- scripts/lib/run-scope.mjs: every run keeps what it makes in its own scope and removes it at the end.
- The Worker's routes and the tests that prove them, under apps/worker/src/features/.

## What to build
1. clients/browser.mjs and the pages it opens, from spike S2's browser client and pages. The pages load posthog-js 1.438.12 from the Worker itself, as a consumer will: `/static/1.438.12/array.full.js` from our host, with its remote config from `/array/<token>/config.js`. Serve the pages from a local page server on another port, so CORS is exercised.
2. Present a visitor's browser, as spike S2's finding 1 explains: Playwright's full Chromium with the automation flag off and no "Headless" in the user agent. The `$pageleave` check runs in a headed browser, because headless Chromium sends no `$pageleave` on a same-tab link click (S2 report, finding 3, checked 2026-10-21). Everything else may run headless.
3. Checks, each named by its behaviour ID, read from the stored rows and R2 objects:
   - config-03, config-05, config-09, config-29: posthog-js loads its config and its lazy scripts from us with no SDK error on the console, and `$autocapture` events carry `$elements_chain`.
   - intake-01, intake-10, intake-11: posthog-js's events are stored, gzip sent as text/plain included.
   - recordings-01, recordings-02: a session's chunks reach R2 and play back in order, and text typed into an input is stored as asterisks.
   - heatmaps-01: `$$heatmap` events become points and no event row.
   - heatmaps-20: after scrolling and a same-tab link click, the stored `$pageleave` carries `$prev_pageview_max_scroll` (headed).
   - cookieless-01: a cookieless page's events are stored under a `cookieless_` id.
4. Register the client so `pnpm compat --only browser` runs it. Close every browser in a finally, so none outlives the run.

You may change apps/compat/ only.

## Your gate
`npx -y pnpm@12.14.0 compat --only browser`
It must exit 0. Also leave `npx -y pnpm@12.14.0 lint` and `npx -y pnpm@12.14.0 typecheck` at exit 0.

## Your final message
What you built; the gate's output lines; anything that does not work and why.
